result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You came to the hospital on 14 October 2026 after a fall at home. You hit your head. You did not lose consciousness.

- Your right hip X-ray showed no fracture (broken bone).
- Your head scan (CT) showed no bleeding inside your head.
- Your blood pressure was 142/80 lying down. It was 108/66 standing up.
- This drop is called postural hypotension. It means your blood pressure drops when you stand up.
- Your medicine amlodipine may be causing this drop. This is possible, not certain.

## What you need to do
1. Stop taking amlodipine 10 milligrams.
2. Do not stop your other medicines. Keep taking them.
3. Stand up slowly.
4. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand.
5. Wait for the Falls Prevention Clinic to write to you with an appointment.
6. Your GP will recheck your blood pressure, lying and standing, in 4 weeks.

## Dates and medicines
- 14 October 2026: you were seen at the hospital.
- In 4 weeks: your GP rechecks your lying and standing blood pressure.
- Amlodipine 10 milligrams: STOP. It may be making your blood pressure drop when you stand.
- All other medicines: keep taking them. No other medicines are named in the letter.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Why should I stop amlodipine?
- When will the Falls Prevention Clinic send my appointment?
- What will happen at my blood pressure check in 4 weeks?

## When to get urgent help
In the next few days, you may get a worsening headache, vomiting, confusion or drowsiness. If you do, call 999 or go to A&E.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
